standard_prerequisites.name: Dimension theory for locally algebraic schemes and generic finiteness
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Varieties, Lemmas lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (tag 0A21) and lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic (tag 0B2L); Morphisms, Lemma morphisms-lemma-generically-finite (tag 02NW)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the generic point of Z is the unique point over the generic point of f(Z) and that f|_Z is generically finite, which makes the degree available.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of higher direct images of a finite morphism and the projection formula
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma coherent-lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent (tag 01Y6); Cohomology, Lemma cohomology-lemma-projection-formula (tag 01E8)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the vanishing of R^i f_*O_Z near xi and the rewriting of the twisted Euler characteristic.

core_obligations: Compute the left-hand side as the coefficient of n_1...n_d in chi(Y, O_Z tensor f^*L_1^{n_1} tensor ... tensor f^*L_d^{n_d}) and rewrite it as the alternating sum over i of chi(X, R^i f_*O_Z tensor L^{n}) via the cited Euler-characteristic morphism lemma and the projection formula (proof lines 10492-10504).

If dim f(Z) < d, observe that the right-hand side is a polynomial of total degree < d by the cited numerical polynomial lemma, so the coefficient vanishes and the statement holds (proof lines 10505-10508).

Assume dim f(Z) = d and let xi be its generic point: use dimension theory to see the generic point of Z is the unique point of Z over xi, and the generic finiteness lemma to conclude f|_Z is finite over an open neighbourhood of xi, so that deg(f|_Z) is defined and equals the length of the stalk of f_*O_Z at xi over O_{X,xi} (proof lines 10508-10517).

Deduce that the higher direct images R^i f_*O_Z vanish at xi for i > 0, so the corresponding Euler characteristics have total degree < d, and compare chi(X, f_*O_Z tensor L^{n}) with the degree times chi(f(Z), L^{n}|_{f(Z)}) modulo lower-degree terms using the leading-term lemma (proof lines 10517-10537).
proof_roadmap: Express the intersection number as a coefficient of an Euler characteristic and expand via higher direct images.
Dispose of the case where the image has smaller dimension by degree reasons.
In the equidimensional case identify the generic fibre with the degree and show higher direct images vanish there.
Compare the two Euler characteristics modulo lower-degree terms.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves (f^*L_1 ... f^*L_d . Z) = deg(f|_Z : Z -> f(Z)) (L_1 ... L_d . f(Z)) for a morphism of proper schemes over k and an integral closed subscheme Z of dimension d. The proof computes the left side as the coefficient of n_1...n_d in an Euler characteristic, rewrites it as the alternating sum of the chi(X, R^i f_*O_Z tensor L^{n}) using a cited Euler-characteristic morphism lemma and the projection formula, and splits into two cases (proof lines 10492-10508). When dim f(Z) < d the total degree is < d and the claim is void; when dim f(Z) = d it uses dimension theory to see the generic point of Z is the unique point over the generic point of f(Z), deduces that f|_Z is generically finite with degree equal to the length of the stalk of f_*O_Z, and kills the higher direct images near that point (proof lines 10508-10536). H2: the generic-finiteness and length identification together with the higher-direct-image vanishing are the non-routine steps.
